problem: Using the method of orthogonal transformations, find the canonical form of $Q(x)={x}_{1}^{2}+6{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}.$
worked_solution:
First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Every quadratic form can be reduced to its canonical (diagonal) form using orthogonal transformations.

To find the coefficients of the canonical form, we need to calculate the eigenvalues of $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 3 \\ 3 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )(1-\lambda )-9 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-2\lambda -8 & =0 \\ (\lambda +2)(\lambda -4) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =4,\,-2\end{aligned}
$$

 

So, writing the eigenvalues in descending order, we obtain the diagonal matrix

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

The corresponding quadratic form after a change of variables is

$$
4{y}_{1}^{2}-2{y}_{2}^{2}.
$$
